regime: Post-FOMC Reversal (Nasdaq Loses Trend, S&P Holds)
summary: The Fed gave the market a spike and then took it back. The Nasdaq ran to a fresh high at 30,180, cleared the 30,000 round, then reversed and closed 29,755, down 0.16 percent, below its trend stop, which flipped to the short side at 30,082. The S&P held better, up 0.06 percent to 7,760.75, still above its stop, so the mirror split. Gold firmed to 4,081.5 (up 0.21 percent) under its 50-hour average, crude reclaimed its stop and jumped 1.71 percent to 101.94, and VIX eased to 16.91.

event.name: FOMC rate decision (Wednesday Oct 28, 2:00 pm ET)
event.consensus: The two-day FOMC meeting concluded Wednesday Oct 28 with the rate decision at 2:00 pm ET and the press conference at 2:30 pm ET. The federal data calendar stays thin under the shutdown, so the Fed was the week's catalyst.
event.actual: A spike-and-reverse. The Nasdaq ran to a new high at 30,180 after the release, then reversed and closed 29,755, down 0.16 percent, losing its trend stop. The S&P held better, up 0.06 percent. Gold and crude firmed; VIX eased.
event.surprise: The first-hour spike failed and unwound, the classic event round trip. The reaction split across assets: equities faded while gold, crude and bonds-proxy risk appetite stayed firm.
event.nqReaction: NQ broke the OR down at 13:45 UTC, reversed up through a 30,180 high on the decision, then rolled over and closed 29,755, below its ATR stop, which flipped short at 30,082.
event.crossAsset: MES plus 0.06 percent at 7,760.75. December gold plus 0.21 percent at 4,081.5. December crude plus 1.71 percent at 101.94. VIX 16.91, down 3.48 percent.

risk.sizing: Measured: 1 micro per strategy, only names above their stops. No new Nasdaq index long until MNQ reclaims 30,082. Lines: MES holds above 7,745; gold above 4,050; crude above 101.45.
risk.openRisk: Measured. The Nasdaq trend-long is off after the stop loss; the S&P and gold longs stay live at small size; crude is a fresh, unconfirmed reclaim.
risk.note: Throttle holds at REDUCED. The Fed is behind us, which removes one binary, but the Nasdaq lost its trend stop on the reversal, so the lead index long is off until price reclaims 30,082. The S&P and gold hold their stops, so those longs stay live at measured size. Crude only just reclaimed its stop, so keep it small until a second close holds above 101.45. No drawdown flags and the loss budget is full. Gold is still under its 4,086 average, so that turn is intact but unconfirmed. Week ahead: tech earnings and the ECB are Thursday's catalysts; watch whether the Nasdaq reclaims its stop or follows through lower.

psychology: Today is a clean example of why you wait for acceptance around a known event. The Fed decision hit, price spiked to a new high, and anyone who chased that breakout got trapped when it reversed. The first move after a release is often a fake. The real direction showed up in the second hour, after the spike failed. If you must trade an event, let two hourly candles close beyond a level before you lean on it. The traders who sat on their hands for the first fifteen minutes kept their capital for the move that actually mattered.

The MNQ, MES and gold hold-above rows all played out as each ran through its upside targets on the Fed spike (MNQ 30,180, MES 7,819.5, gold 4,097.3), though MNQ then reversed and lost its stop. The crude stay-below-short row failed as crude reclaimed 101.89 and rallied 1.71 percent. The MNQ down-path row did not trigger because price held above 29,547 all day.
